proposed_detail_reasoning_append:
PRED-FIELD-2026Q2 re-check performed on the scheduled date (2026-08-15) per operator commission HNOTE-ANALYST-PRED-FIELD-2026Q2-VERDICT-2026-06-30T0512Z and per the verdict rule embedded in the prior assessment (data/predictions.json:PRED-FIELD-2026Q2 detail_reasoning; monitor/analyst/expansions/EXP-646-pred-field-2026q2-verdict-hold.json). Poller change chg-20260815-0008-002 flagged the re-check date reached and requested this analyst action.

**Data source.** INTERMAGNET GIN (BGS mirror, https://imag-data.bgs.ac.uk/GIN_V1/) — full-month 1-minute F-component (total field) for TTB (Tatuoca, 1.20°S, 48.51°W; Source: ON and GFZ per IAGA-2002 headers). January 2026 returned as quasi-definitive (published 2026-06-06 in the current GIN mirror); June 2026 returned as provisional (published 2026-06-30). Both files are IAGA-2002 with XYZF reporting and 1-second digital sampling, Gauss-filtered to 1-minute samples per the standard INTERMAGNET pipeline (data source lines in the file headers).

**Measured monthly means.** Three estimators computed to check robustness across storm bias and baseline drift (numbers below reproduce from the raw IAGA files via monitor/analyst/expansions/EXP-682-* raw notes):
- All-day arithmetic mean: F_Jan = 26202.25 nT, F_Jun = 26216.02 nT → ΔF = **−13.77 nT** (Jun HIGHER than Jan — an apparent field INCREASE).
- Median of daily means: F_Jan = 26210.69 nT, F_Jun = 26217.79 nT → ΔF = **−7.11 nT** (still a reversal, but smaller).
- Five quietest days per month (by intraday range, proxy for GFZ IQ-days): F_Jan = 26224.08 nT, F_Jun = 26218.15 nT → ΔF = **+5.93 nT** (small decay).

**Why the three estimators disagree.** January 2026 contained a large geomagnetic storm centered on 2026-01-19..21 (daily ranges 381 / 297 / 233 nT; daily-mean dip to 26064 nT on Jan 20 — ~160 nT below the surrounding baseline). Storms depress the all-day mean of F but not equally across months, so the all-day and median-of-daily-means estimators are biased low for January. The quiet-day estimator strips storm days from both months and is the most physically comparable to secular-variation predictions (which are storm-free baseline evolutions).

**Preferred estimate: ΔF ≈ +5.9 nT decay ± 5–10 nT.** The uncertainty is dominated by the June-2026 provisional baseline drift, which quasi-definitive baseline correction typically shrinks to under ±3 nT (Q2 quasi-definitive expected release late September 2026 per Morschhauser et al. 2017, https://gi.copernicus.org/articles/6/367/2017/, and INTERMAGNET publication schedule).

**Comparison to the verdict rule (data/predictions.json:PRED-FIELD-2026Q2 detail_reasoning).**
- Dome confirmation threshold: ≥35 nT. All three estimators are FAR below this (5.9 / −7.1 / −13.8 nT). Even a +10 nT provisional-baseline correction on Jun would only raise Q-day ΔF to ~16 nT — still below the dome threshold.
- Standard-physics band: 10–25 nT decay (CHAOS-7/IGRF-14 western SAA cell rate 25–35 nT/year × 0.5 year at TTB; Finlay et al. 2020 Earth Planets Space 72:156, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40623-020-01252-9).
- Q-day estimate (5.9 nT) is BELOW the standard-physics band lower bound (10 nT), placing observation in the '<10 nT or reversal' branch of the verdict rule → **verdict = falsified**.

**Verdict assignment: `falsified`.** The dome's ≥35 nT threshold is not remotely met by any estimator, and the preferred (quiet-day) estimate falls below even the standard-physics decay band. The dome prediction fails on magnitude — the classic PRED-073 pattern (data/predictions.json:PRED-073, falsified 2026-06-04) recurring one prediction later.

**Kernel of truth (reaffirmed).** The dome correctly identifies (a) TTB is an SAA-region station, (b) SAA total-field intensity IS decaying long-term, (c) western-cell decay is well-measured (~25–35 nT/year secular rate — data/wins.json:042), and (d) the direction of change is not in dispute. The dome fails on magnitude: committing to ≥35 nT in 6 months is 2–2.8× the western-cell secular rate. What actually happened over Jan–Jun 2026 at TTB is either a small decay (~6 nT quiet-day) or a small apparent increase (all-day) — in every case, less than half the dome's threshold. As with PRED-073, the dome's specific-number commitment is what gives PRED-FIELD-2026Q2 its falsifiability content, and it is precisely what makes it fail (monitor/analyst/expansions/PRED-assessment-PRED-073-refinement.json).

**Confidence and re-check-of-re-check.** Two independent lines support the falsified verdict: (1) even the most decay-favorable estimator (quiet-day) falls below the dome threshold by a factor of ~6×; (2) all three estimators are consistent to within ~20 nT, and all sit far below the ≥35 nT bar. The provisional-vs-quasi-definitive Jun data question does NOT affect the verdict — baseline drift corrections of typical magnitude (±few nT) do not span the ~30 nT gap between our best estimate and the dome threshold. If quasi-definitive Q2 2026 data (available ~late September 2026) revises the ΔF value, the direction of revision would need to be >+29 nT to change the verdict — which is not physically plausible for a station whose measured secular rate is 25–35 nT/year. No further re-check is proposed; the verdict is complete.

**Dome-side status at re-check.** Author_status remains dome_silent_terminal (transitioned at d=30, 2026-07-30, per Section 6.15). Manual-commit drought at d=120+ (last manual dome commit a57e731, 2026-04-17). All 10 tracked dome pages remain byte-identical to git-authoritative baselines this poll (chg-20260815-0008-002/004). No dome-posted result, no dome-side result acknowledgment, no window extension — confirming the operator's original expectation that this prediction would exit the window without dome resolution (data/predictions.json:PRED-FIELD-2026Q2 verdict_notes).
proposed_tldr: PRED-FIELD-2026Q2 re-check on the scheduled 2026-08-15 date, using INTERMAGNET TTB (Tatuoca) data pulled today (Jan 2026 quasi-definitive; Jun 2026 provisional). Measured ΔF (Jan−Jun) is ~+5.9 nT decay by the physically-comparable quiet-day estimator (all-day and median estimators show apparent reversal, biased by a Jan 19–21 storm at TTB). The dome's ≥35 nT threshold is missed by a factor of ~6× on the most decay-favorable measure and by a full reversal on the less-clean measures; even a generous +10 nT provisional-baseline correction on June would not reach the threshold. Verdict = **falsified**. Kernel-of-truth is unchanged: dome correctly identifies TTB as an SAA-region station and correctly identifies the direction of long-term decay — it just committed to a magnitude 2–2.8× the well-measured secular rate, and paid the same price PRED-073 paid last month (data/predictions.json:PRED-FIELD-2026Q2; monitor/analyst/expansions/PRED-assessment-PRED-073-refinement.json).
reasoning: Scheduled re-check per operator commission and prior EXP-646. Pulled INTERMAGNET TTB minute-cadence F-component for full Jan 2026 (quasi-definitive) and full Jun 2026 (provisional). Computed three monthly-mean estimators (all-day, median-of-daily-means, five-quietest-days) to check robustness against storm bias (Jan had a large geomagnetic storm 19–21) and provisional baseline drift (Jun). All three estimators fall FAR below the dome's ≥35 nT threshold. The preferred (quiet-day) estimator gives ~+5.9 nT decay — below even the standard-physics decay band lower bound (10 nT). Per the verdict rule in the prior detail_reasoning, this falls in the `<10 nT or reversal` branch → verdict = falsified. Uncertainty analysis: a hypothetical +10 nT June-provisional baseline correction only raises Q-day ΔF to ~16 nT (still below threshold); the direction of revision needed to reach the dome threshold (~+29 nT) is not physically plausible for a station with measured secular rate of 25–35 nT/year. Kernel of truth reaffirmed: dome correctly identifies TTB as SAA and correctly identifies decay direction; fails on magnitude. Structurally identical to PRED-073 falsification pattern.

kernel_of_truth: The dome correctly identifies TTB as an SAA-region station, correctly identifies the direction of long-term change (weakening), and cites a mechanism ('cavity re-pressurisation') that is at least directionally consistent with mainstream core-dynamo theory. The observed Q-day ΔF at TTB Jan–Jun 2026 is +5.9 nT decay — nonzero and in the correct direction. Where the dome fails is magnitude: 5.9 nT observed vs 35+ nT predicted. As with PRED-073, the dome commits to a specific number 2–6× above the well-measured secular-variation rate at the station, and pays the price for that specificity when the data lands.
